problemStatement.formal: theorem alternating_triangular_sum : HasSum (fun n : Nat => if n = 0 then 0 else (-1 : Real) ^ (n + 1) * (2 / (n * (n + 1)))) (4 * Real.log 2 - 2)
problemStatement.plain: Prove the alternating sum of reciprocals of triangular numbers: sum (-1)^(n+1) * 2/(n(n+1)) = 4*log(2) - 2.
whyMatters: Extends the classical telescoping result ∑2/(n(n+1)) = 2 to its alternating variant
Demonstrates that alternating figurate reciprocals yield transcendental values
Connects triangular numbers to the natural logarithm via the Mercator series

proven: alternating_triangular_sum proves the alternating triangular reciprocal series equals 4*log(2)-2, using two alternating-harmonic axioms.
summable_alt_triangular proves summability of the alternating triangular reciprocal series.
tsum versions of the main result and corollary are included.
open: Prove the alternating harmonic series identities without axioms.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Proofs/TriangularReciprocalAlternatingOQ03.lean proves the alternating triangular reciprocal series with 0 sorries and 2 axioms for the alternating harmonic series. Source audit: 165 lines, 5 theorems, 0 definitions, 2 axioms, 0 sorries.
insights: The shifted alternating harmonic ∑(-1)^{n+1}/(n+1) = 1-ln(2) follows from the standard series by removing first term
HasSum.mul_left and HasSum.sub compose cleanly for combining scaled series
funext + by_cases is the right approach for HasSum function rewriting (not HasSum.congr, which produces finset sum goals)
The alternating sum 4·ln(2)-2 ≈ 0.7726 is transcendental, unlike the non-alternating sum which equals exactly 2
